name: HomeListingAI

prices.note: $79 a month; $49 founding price for the first 25 loan officers

rules: Plain words, short punchy lines, one idea. No statistics except the verified facts listed in this brief, if any. No other numbers about Realtors, no customer stories, no guaranteed referrals or closings. Never say "never miss a lead" or "no lead goes cold". Never say the product finds, matches or supplies Realtors: it gives the loan officer a free WOW Link listing page to bring to an agent, and the buyer chat sends the warm lead to the loan officer.

nar-members-now.text: NAR membership was about 1.44 million in June 2026, roughly 10% below its peak of about 1.6 million in October 2022.

nar-members-one-year.text: NAR membership fell about 1.7% in one year, from about 1.46 million to about 1.44 million (June 2025 to June 2026).

sole-vocation.text: In a 2025 survey, 71% of NAR members said real estate is their only job, the lowest share since 2005, and newer and younger agents were the ones leaving.

topics.idea: A WOW Link is a free listing page you send an agent. It answers buyer questions all day and the warm lead comes to you. Show a loan officer the simplest way to give an agent something useful this week.

Agents love free help that makes their listing look better. A WOW Link gives them a page with an AI chat on it, at no cost to them. Frame it as what a loan officer can bring to an agent that is not a rate sheet.
Most loan officers show up to agents with a rate sheet. Agents already have one. Talk about showing up with something that helps them sell a listing instead.
Buyers browse listings at night and on weekends, when nobody answers. The listing page chat answers them and captures a name and phone number for the loan officer.
A cold lead is a name on a list. A warm lead raised their hand about a real home. Explain the difference in plain words and where warm leads come from.
The first call to a new lead matters most. The app tells the loan officer who to call next, with the lead in front of them. Keep it practical.
The Today screen shows one lead to call next. One screen, one action. Talk about not having to dig through a pipeline to find the right call.
The AI phone line answers when the loan officer cannot, gets a name and number, and passes it along. It works beside the loan officer, not instead of them. The AI tells callers it is an AI.
Train the AI Brain once and every listing chat and phone call uses it. Your rules, your answers, your voice. Teach it once.
AI is a teammate, not a replacement. It covers the gaps: the night, the weekend, the busy day. The loan officer still closes the loan.
The Share Kit gives a loan officer a listing link, a QR code, a flyer and a ready social post for any listing, in one place. No design work.
Put a QR code on a sign rider or flyer and buyers can chat with the listing from the sidewalk. Talk about turning a yard sign into a lead source.
Try it for 7 days, no card. Send one WOW Link to one agent and see what happens. Low risk, one small step.
Challenge: send one WOW Link to one agent. Just one. Small actions beat big plans.
Condo rules keep changing. Condo Check reads an association document and pulls out the facts with the page and quote so the loan officer can check them. Say the loan officer confirms every fact.
A live dashboard for each listing shows the leads it brought in. A loan officer can share it with the agent so both see the same thing.
Sharing marketing costs with an agent gets awkward. The invoice tool lets a loan officer send a clean invoice. The app never touches the money.
Stop adding software. Add help. A loan officer does not need another dashboard to check. They need leads that show up with a name and a number.
Agents send deals to the loan officer who makes them look good. Give them a reason that is more than rates and fast closings.
A listing with an AI chat looks modern. Sellers notice. The agent can say it is part of how they market homes. Position it as a listing edge for the agent.
Loan officers lose hours to repeat questions: what documents, how long, what costs. Let the AI handle the repeat questions so the loan officer spends time on real conversations.
The listing page shows the loan officer NMLS, Equal Housing and a not-a-commitment note, and the AI says it is an AI. Compliance should not be an afterthought.
Buyers want answers before they want to talk to anyone. Give them answers first, then a human. That is how a buyer becomes a conversation.
In a slow market, agents work harder for every showing. A loan officer who helps a listing get more serious buyer questions becomes the loan officer the agent calls first.
Set up takes minutes: add your details, send a WOW Link, publish a listing. Say what the first week looks like in three plain steps.

launch.headline: Your referral network is changing. What's your plan?
launch.idea: Campaign 1, The Disappearing Network. Open with: Your referral network is changing. Say plainly that some Realtor partners have slowed down or left the industry, and that your network may not be producing like it used to. Never say all or most Realtors are leaving. What is your plan? No numbers. End with a clear next step. {{RULES}}

launch.headline: You can't control the market. You can control how you compete.
launch.idea: You cannot control rates. You cannot control the housing market. You cannot stop Realtors from leaving. But you can control how you compete. Build the post on that turn. {{RULES}}

launch.headline: Is your referral network still producing?
launch.idea: Depending on yesterday's referral network is a risk. Ask the loan officer when they last added a new agent partner, and why. Honest and direct, no scare tactics. {{RULES}}

launch.headline: Waiting for rates is not a plan.
launch.idea: Waiting for rates to fall is not a business development plan. Say what to do this week instead: start one new agent relationship. {{RULES}}

launch.headline: Your competition is building new relationships. Are you?
launch.idea: Campaign 2, Your Competition Is Not Waiting. Your competition is building new relationships. Are you? Say that loan officers who keep adding agent partners have more doors open, without any numbers or names. {{RULES}}

launch.headline: Doing nothing is a risk.
launch.idea: The cost of doing nothing: every referral you never get because the agent does not know you exist. Show the consequence in plain words and give one small step. {{RULES}}

launch.headline: What if two of your top agents slow down?
launch.idea: Most loan officers lean on the same few agents. Ask what happens to the pipeline if two of them slow down. Then point to starting one new relationship. {{RULES}}

launch.headline: Stop showing up with a rate sheet.
launch.idea: Every loan officer shows up with a rate sheet. Competitors who show up with something that helps the agent sell a listing get remembered. Use that contrast. {{RULES}}

launch.headline: Your next top Realtor partner doesn't know you exist.
launch.idea: Campaign 3, The Opportunity. Your next top Realtor partner does not know you exist. Show how to start: send them a free WOW Link, a listing page with an AI buyer chat, for one of their listings. {{RULES}}

launch.headline: Send one WOW Link. Start the conversation.
launch.idea: Explain a WOW Link in three plain steps: you send it, the agent previews a page for their listing, buyers chat with it and the warm lead comes to you. Real steps only. {{RULES}}

launch.headline: Start with something useful, not a pitch.
launch.idea: Start the relationship with something useful instead of a pitch. A free listing page that answers buyers at night and on weekends is useful to an agent. Say it that simply. {{RULES}}

launch.headline: A name. A phone number. A warm lead.
launch.idea: The payoff for the loan officer is a warm lead: a buyer who asked about a real home and left a name and a phone number. Describe that moment. Do not promise a number of leads. {{RULES}}

launch.headline: Founding price: $49 a month. First 25 loan officers.
launch.idea: Founding loan officer launch price: $49 a month instead of $79 for the first 25 loan officers who join, with a 7-day free trial and no card. It ends when the 25 spots are gone. Do not invent a date. Call to action: claim your founding price. {{RULES}}

launch.headline: Stop waiting for the market to save you.
launch.idea: Stop waiting for the market to save you. Start building your next referral network. Finish with a direct call to action to start the free trial. {{RULES}}

launch.headline: Try it free for 7 days. Send one WOW Link.
launch.idea: Low risk: start the 7-day free trial, send one WOW Link to one agent, and see what happens. Keep it small and clear. {{RULES}}

launch.headline: The market changed. It's time you did too.
launch.idea: The market changed. It is time you did too. Build your network. Build your pipeline. Build your future. A confident closing post that ends with the free trial. {{RULES}}

writer.note: What the AI video writer is told. A copy for another business rewrites this section: intro, abilities, the variety lists and each scene's prompt.
writer.intro: You write the words for a short animated explainer video for HomeListingAI, a tool that helps loan officers win agent partnerships and get warm buyer leads. The viewer is a loan officer. Plain words, no hype. Never quote or hint at rates, approvals, pre-approvals or guarantees. Never promise results. No statistics unless they are in the verified list. No real people, banks or brands.
abilities: A WOW Link is a free listing page the loan officer sends to a real estate agent. Buyers chat with it and warm leads come to the loan officer.
The buyer chat on a listing page answers questions, says plainly it is an AI, and sends the buyer's name and number to the loan officer.
The AI phone line answers calls for the loan officer, says plainly it is an AI, takes a name and number and passes them along.
The AI Brain is where the loan officer teaches the AI once and every listing uses it.
The Share Kit gives a listing a link, a QR code, a flyer and a social post.
The partner dashboard shows the loan officer which agents opened their WOW Link.
The plan has a 7-day free trial with no card. It is $79 a month, and $49 a month founding price for the first 25 loan officers.

buyer-chat.prompt: Scene: a buyer browses a SAMPLE home listing page at the given time, after the loan officer's office has closed. The listing page's AI assistant answers a believable question that fits the post, and says plainly that it is an AI. It offers two ways to follow up, the buyer picks the first, and a warm lead goes to the loan officer. Fields: business (the sample listing, like "Palm Ave condo", under 18 characters, no word Sample); closedLine (under 50 characters, why the office is closed at that time); timeLabel and timeSuffix (the given time, like "11:38" and "PM"); question (under 70 characters, a real question a buyer asks that fits the post, no rates); answer (under 85 characters, starts with "I am an AI." and answers plainly, no numbers); optionA and optionB (follow-up choices under 12 characters, like "Call me" and "Text me"); booked (under 38 characters, says a loan officer will reach out); leadTitle (under 34 characters, like "Warm lead sent to the loan officer"); leadLine1 to leadLine3 (under 34 characters each, what was captured).

ai-phone.prompt: Scene: a SAMPLE loan officer's AI phone line answers a call while the loan officer is busy. The caller is the given kind of buyer and asks something that fits the post. The AI says plainly it is an AI, takes a name and number for the loan officer, and a warm lead is saved. Fields: callerLabel ("Unknown caller" or similar, under 20 characters); hook1 and hook2 (an opening line in two parts, each under 22 characters, that fits the post); hookAccent (the last words of hook2); callerSays1 (under 65 characters, a believable request, no rates); aiSays1 (under 75 characters, starts with "I am an AI" and asks for a name and number); callerSays2 (under 30 characters, gives a first name and a number like "Sam, 555-0142"); aiSays2 (under 50 characters, says a loan officer will call soon); leadTitle (under 34 characters, like "Warm lead sent to the loan officer"); leadLine1 to leadLine3 (under 34 characters each).

wow-link.prompt: Scene: a guided walkthrough of ONE real feature, the given one. An app on a phone takes a loan officer through three steps. In each step the guide says what to do, a sample value is typed into a field, and a green result appears. Fields: hook1 and hook2 (an opening line in two parts, each under 22 characters, that fits the post); hookAccent (the last words of hook2); guideName (the feature's name, under 26 characters, like "WOW Link guide"); for each of step1, step2 and step3: Says (what the guide says, under 60 characters), Label (the field name in capitals, under 20 characters), Value (a sample value typed in, under 38 characters, no real people or brands), Result (what appears when it is done, under 34 characters). The three steps must be real steps of that feature and use only the approved abilities.

plan.prompt: Scene: a plan card on a phone. The plan name and its price appear, then four things it includes are ticked off one at a time, then up to two small promises. It must say what the post says. Fields: hook1 and hook2 (an opening line in two parts, each under 22 characters, that fits the post); hookAccent (the last words of hook2); planName (under 24 characters, like "Loan officer plan"); price (exactly as on the approved price list, like "$79/month" or "$49/month"); item1 to item4 (what the plan includes, each under 30 characters, only approved abilities, in the order the post gives them); perk1 and perk2 (small promises the post makes, like "7-day free trial" and "No card to start", each under 24 characters, only if the post says them, otherwise leave perk2 empty).

listing-chat.prompt: Scene: a buyer asks the AI assistant on ONE real home's listing page, late in the evening after the loan officer's office has closed. The POST TEXT lists the only facts that exist about this home. The question must be about one of those facts, or about how to ask about the home. The answer must say "I am an AI." first and then use ONLY those facts (bedrooms, baths, price, address). Never mention the neighborhood, schools, taxes, condition, rates or what the buyer can afford. Fields: closedLine (under 50 characters, why the office is closed at that time); timeLabel and timeSuffix (the given time, like "9:15" and "PM"); question (under 70 characters); answer (under 85 characters, starts with "I am an AI." and uses only the given facts); optionA and optionB (follow-up choices under 12 characters, like "Call me" and "Text me").

look.note: The look of every picture. Palette, art-director voice, lighting, banned content, scene ideas. A copy for another business edits this section (and logo.png).
look.director: You are the visual creative director for HomeListingAI, a business-growth platform marketed to mortgage loan officers and brokers. Make premium, high-contrast, cinematic images. One concept per image. Dark charcoal composition, selective cyan/lime, violet/coral, cobalt/pink, blue/yellow or turquoise/magenta accents, detailed homes, conceptual sculptures and professionals, legible on a phone. Lead with loan officer growth and building new Realtor relationships. Never show a fake dashboard, robot, invented logo or readable text. Never say all or most Realtors are leaving.
look.lighting: Dramatic, lifelike lighting: deep navy shadows, saturated topic-specific cyan, lime, violet, coral, cobalt, pink or yellow edge light, a confident optimistic finish. Modern American real-estate and mortgage business setting, believable, precise focus, restrained sophistication, premium commercial photography.
look.negative: No embedded text, no logos, no fabricated interface screenshots, no watermarks, no stock-art look, no unrealistic anatomy, no robots, no handshake clichés.
look.editorialStyle: Premium editorial advertising artwork, realistic architecture or tactile conceptual 3D miniatures. Topic-relevant glass brains, bridges, connected homes and chess pieces are welcome. Deep navy background with selective cyan/lime, violet/coral, cobalt/pink, blue/yellow or turquoise/magenta accents. Clear subject, visible detail. Avoid repeated orange doorways and silhouettes.
look.launchLook: Premium editorial advertising artwork: tactile 3D miniature homes or realistic architecture, deep navy background, saturated selective accent lighting, one clear visual metaphor related to the headline. Square frame: hero subject in the lower half, upper 40 percent calm and dark for a large headline. Never muddy or underexposed. No repeated orange doorway or lonely silhouette.
look.brightLook: Bright editorial photograph, natural golden-hour light, welcoming modern real-estate setting, clear subject related to the article, uncluttered space on the left.
look.extraRules: No readable text, letters, numbers or logos anywhere. No signs, house numbers, labels or writing. No screens showing an interface, invented results, rates, charts or customer claims. No identifiable faces. Conceptual glass brains are allowed for AI topics; miniature homes, bridges and chess pieces are allowed when relevant. Do not imply these illustrations show actual listings.
